items.stem: What happens when a magnet is held still inside a coil?
items.answer: No potential difference is induced
items.markingKey: D. There must be relative motion.

items.stem: Elena writes: "A magnet near a coil always produces a current." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: A current is only induced while the magnetic field through the coil is changing (movement or changing field) and the circuit is complete.
items.markingKey: A current is only induced while the magnetic field through the coil is changing (movement or changing field) and the circuit is complete. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why more turns on a coil give a larger induced voltage.
items.answer: Each turn has a voltage induced in it; the turns are in series so the voltages add. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Each turn has a voltage induced in it; the turns are in series so the voltages add. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

Number of turns | Peak voltage / mV: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3

items.stem: Ana is investigating how the speed at which a magnet falls through a coil affects the peak induced voltage. Formulate a testable hypothesis and justify it using scientific knowledge.
items.answer: If the drop height increases, then the peak voltage will increase, because the magnet moves faster through the coil, so the magnetic field changes more rapidly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: testable prediction in "if … then …" form linking the independent and dependent variables; 1-2 marks: scientific explanation. Model: If the drop height increases, then the peak voltage will increase, because the magnet moves faster through the coil, so the magnetic field changes more rapidly.

items.stem: A magnet pushed into a coil at a certain speed induces a peak voltage of 0.3 V. Predict the voltage if the magnet moves 4 times as fast, and explain.
items.answer: 1.2 V; the magnetic field through the coil changes 4 times as fast
items.markingKey: M1 voltage ∝ rate of change of flux; A1 1.2 V; B1 explanation.

items.stem: Describe an experiment to show the factors affecting the size of the voltage induced when a magnet moves through a coil, and explain the results using the idea of rate of change of magnetic field.
items.answer: Connect coil to a sensitive voltmeter/data logger; drop or push a magnet through; vary speed (drop height), number of turns, magnet strength; record peak voltage; repeat. Larger speed, more turns, stronger magnet → larger voltage, because the magnetic flux through the coil changes faster/by more, and each turn adds voltage. Direction reverses as magnet leaves or when poles reversed (Lenz).
items.markingKey: Connect coil to a sensitive voltmeter/data logger; drop or push a magnet through; vary speed (drop height), number of turns, magnet strength; record peak voltage; repeat. Direction reverses as magnet leaves or when poles reversed (Lenz).

items.stem: Write a risk assessment for an investigation into how the speed at which a magnet falls through a coil affects the peak induced voltage. Identify two hazards, the risk each poses and how each risk will be reduced, and explain one ethical or environmental consideration.
items.answer: Key hazard(s): strong magnets can trap fingers; keep away from electronic devices and pacemakers. For each hazard: state what could go wrong, how likely/serious it is, and the precaution. Ethical/environmental: e.g. minimise waste and dispose of chemicals correctly, treat living organisms and volunteers with respect and consent.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "Faraday’s law".
items.answer: The induced voltage is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage

items.stem: Distinguish between an induced current and an induced voltage.
items.answer: An induced voltage is produced whenever the flux through a conductor changes; an induced current flows only if the conductor is part of a complete circuit.
items.markingKey: An induced voltage is produced whenever the flux through a conductor changes; an induced current flows only if the conductor is part of a complete circuit. items.stem: Explain how a dynamo on a bicycle produces electricity.
items.answer: The wheel turns a magnet near a coil; the changing magnetic field through the coil induces an alternating voltage that lights the lamp.

items.answer: As the coil rotates, the rate at which it cuts magnetic field lines changes smoothly – maximum when the coil is parallel to the field and zero when perpendicular – and reverses each half turn.

items.stem: Briefly describe The “War of the Currents” (1880s–1890s) and explain what it reveals about ac vs dc.
items.answer: Edison promoted dc power; Tesla and Westinghouse promoted ac; ac won because transformers allowed efficient long-distance transmission. Today high-voltage dc (HVDC) is used again for very long cables, showing technology choices change.

items.stem: Describe the structure of a simple ac generator and explain how it produces an alternating voltage. Describe how the output trace on an oscilloscope changes if the coil rotates twice as fast.
items.answer: Rectangular coil rotating between poles of a magnet; ends connected to slip rings with brushes. Rotation changes the flux through the coil → induced voltage; direction reverses every half turn → ac sine wave. Twice as fast: twice the frequency (half the period, cycles closer together) and twice the peak voltage (taller wave).

Ingrid measured the efficiency of a demonstration transformer at different output currents (three trials).

Output current / A | Efficiency / %: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3

0.6 | 98 | 98 | 100

items.stem: Explain how a transformer works, and use calculations to show why transmitting 100 MW at 400 kV rather than at 25 kV reduces power losses in a cable of resistance 5 Ω.
items.answer: Alternating current in primary → changing magnetic field in iron core → changing flux through secondary → induced alternating voltage; Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. At 25 kV: I = 100 × 10⁶ / 25 000 = 4000 A, loss = 4000² × 5 = 80 MW (impractical). At 400 kV: I = 250 A, loss = 250² × 5 = 312 500 W ≈ 0.31 MW. Higher voltage → lower current → much lower I²R loss.

items.stem: Using The “War of the Currents” (1880s–1890s) as an example, explain ac vs dc.
items.answer: Edison promoted dc power; Tesla and Westinghouse promoted ac; ac won because transformers allowed efficient long-distance transmission. Today high-voltage dc (HVDC) is used again for very long cables, showing technology choices change.
items.markingKey: Context (Edison promoted dc power; Tesla and Westinghouse promoted ac; ac won because transformers allowed efficient long-distance transmission.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Today high-voltage dc (HVDC) is used again for very long cables, showing technology choices change. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to ac vs dc.

items.stem: With reference to Smart grids and interconnectors, explain how it illustrates modern grid design.
items.answer: Undersea interconnectors link national grids (e.g. Norway–UK North Sea Link, 2021) so countries can share surplus renewable electricity. Helps balance intermittent renewables over larger areas.
items.markingKey: Context (Undersea interconnectors link national grids (e.g. Norway–UK North Sea Link, 2021) so countries can share surplus renewable electricity.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Helps balance intermittent renewables over larger areas. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to modern grid design.

items.stem: Design a safe and valid method to investigate how the rotation frequency of a hand-cranked ac generator affects the frequency and peak voltage of its output. In your answer include the variables, the equipment, the range and number of values of the independent variable, the number of repeats, safety and how the data will be recorded and processed.
items.answer: Connect the generator across a 10 Ω resistor to a data logger; crank at each rate with a metronome for 10 s; from the trace measure the period of several cycles and the peak voltage; calculate frequency; repeat three times; plot both against cranking rate.
items.markingKey: MYP criterion B: 1 independent variable with at least 5 values in a sensible range; 1 dependent variable and how it is measured; 1 at least two controls and how they are controlled; 1 logical step-by-step procedure with equipment; 1 at least 3 repeats and calculation of a mean; 1 relevant safety point (secure the generator; low voltages only; keep loose clothing away from moving parts). Model: Connect the generator across a 10 Ω resistor to a data logger; crank at each rate with a metronome for 10 s; from the trace measure the period of several cycles and the peak voltage; calculate frequency; repeat three times; plot both against cranking rate.

items.stem: Ingrid plans an investigation into how the number of turns on the secondary coil of a demonstration transformer affects the output voltage. Describe how the results should be recorded, processed and presented, and explain how the reliability and validity of the conclusion will be judged.
items.answer: Results table with the independent variable (number of secondary turns (100, 200, 300, 400, 500) with 200 primary turns) in the first column and repeat readings of the dependent variable with units in headings; calculate means (ignoring anomalies); plot a suitable graph of the mean dependent variable against the independent variable with a line of best fit; describe the trend and compare with the hypothesis; judge reliability from the spread of repeats and validity from how well variables were controlled.
items.markingKey: 1 table with IV, repeats and units; 1 means calculated, anomalies identified and excluded; 1 appropriate graph (line graph/scatter for continuous IV, bar chart for categorical) with line of best fit; 1 trend compared with hypothesis; 1 reliability (spread of repeats) and validity (controls) discussed.

items.stem: Design a safe and valid method to investigate how the speed at which a magnet falls through a coil affects the peak induced voltage. In your answer include the variables, the equipment, the range and number of values of the independent variable, the number of repeats, safety and how the data will be recorded and processed.
items.answer: Clamp a coil around a vertical plastic tube; connect to a data logger at 1000 samples/s; drop the magnet from rest from each height through the tube onto a cushion; record the peak voltage; repeat five times; calculate speed √(2gh) and plot peak voltage against speed.
items.markingKey: MYP criterion B: 1 independent variable with at least 5 values in a sensible range; 1 dependent variable and how it is measured; 1 at least two controls and how they are controlled; 1 logical step-by-step procedure with equipment; 1 at least 3 repeats and calculation of a mean; 1 relevant safety point (strong magnets can trap fingers; keep away from electronic devices and pacemakers). Model: Clamp a coil around a vertical plastic tube; connect to a data logger at 1000 samples/s; drop the magnet from rest from each height through the tube onto a cushion; record the peak voltage; repeat five times; calculate speed √(2gh) and plot peak voltage against speed.

items.stem: "High-voltage dc links should replace ac for long-distance and undersea transmission." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: HVDC is best for very long or undersea links; ac remains best for most local grids.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: lower losses over very long distances and in undersea cables; can link grids with different frequencies. Arguments against: converter stations are expensive; ac is simpler for local distribution. Supported judgement: HVDC is best for very long or undersea links; ac remains best for most local grids. Markbands (15 marks): MYP criterion D (0-8, scaled): 7-8 explains thoroughly how the science is applied to address the issue, discusses and evaluates the implications (moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural or environmental), and documents sources consistently; 5-6 explains and discusses; 3-4 outlines; 1-2 states.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Faraday’s law"?
options: A device with two coils on an iron core that changes the size of an alternating voltage
The induced voltage is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage
A measure of the amount of magnetic field passing through an area
The production of a potential difference across a conductor when it moves relative to a magnetic field, or when the field through it changes
items.answer: The induced voltage is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage
items.markingKey: B. "Faraday’s law" is the induced voltage is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "peak voltage"?
options: A measure of the amount of magnetic field passing through an area
Rings in an ac generator that keep a continuous connection with the rotating coil without reversing
The maximum voltage reached in an ac cycle
An induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the change that caused it
items.answer: The maximum voltage reached in an ac cycle
items.markingKey: C. "peak voltage" is the maximum voltage reached in an ac cycle.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "transformer"?
options: Current that flows in one direction only, e.g. from a cell
A device with two coils on an iron core that changes the size of an alternating voltage
The induced voltage is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage
An induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the change that caused it
items.answer: A device with two coils on an iron core that changes the size of an alternating voltage
items.markingKey: B. "transformer" is a device with two coils on an iron core that changes the size of an alternating voltage.

items.stem: A student claims: "A magnet near a coil always produces a current." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: A current is only induced while the magnetic field through the coil is changing (movement or changing field) and the circuit is complete.
items.markingKey: A current is only induced while the magnetic field through the coil is changing (movement or changing field) and the circuit is complete. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between dc and ac.
items.answer: ac repeatedly reverses direction (sine wave on an oscilloscope); dc flows in one direction only (a horizontal line).
items.markingKey: ac repeatedly reverses direction (sine wave on an oscilloscope); dc flows in one direction only (a horizontal line). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between a step-down transformer and a step-up transformer.
items.answer: A step-up transformer has more secondary than primary turns and increases voltage (decreasing current); a step-down has fewer secondary turns and decreases voltage (increasing current).
items.markingKey: A step-up transformer has more secondary than primary turns and increases voltage (decreasing current); a step-down has fewer secondary turns and decreases voltage (increasing current). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Leila writes: "Generators create electrical energy from nothing." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Generators transfer kinetic energy into electrical energy; work must be done to turn them.
items.markingKey: Generators transfer kinetic energy into electrical energy; work must be done to turn them. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a split-ring commutator and slip rings.
items.answer: Slip rings keep the same coil end connected to the same brush, giving ac; a split ring swaps the connections every half turn, giving dc.
items.markingKey: Slip rings keep the same coil end connected to the same brush, giving ac; a split ring swaps the connections every half turn, giving dc. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Sana writes: "Transformers work with batteries." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Batteries supply dc, which does not produce a changing magnetic field, so no voltage is induced in the secondary.
items.markingKey: Batteries supply dc, which does not produce a changing magnetic field, so no voltage is induced in the secondary. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Lukas measured the peak voltage induced when a magnet was dropped through coils with different numbers of turns (three drops each).

Number of turns | Peak voltage / mV: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
50 | 54 | 51 | 52
100 | 102 | 103 | 107
150 | 154 | 151 | 151
200 | 205 | 209 | 206
250 | 272 | 268 | 270

Describe the trend shown by the results and explain it using scientific knowledge.
items.answer: The peak induced voltage increases in direct proportion to the number of turns. The same change in magnetic field induces the same voltage in each turn; the turns are in series so the voltages add.
items.markingKey: 1 trend: The peak induced voltage increases in direct proportion to the number of turns.; 1 use of data (quote means/values); 1-2 explanation: The same change in magnetic field induces the same voltage in each turn; the turns are in series so the voltages add.

items.stem: An ac supply has a period of 0.05 s. Calculate its frequency.
items.answer: 20 Hz

items.stem:
Mohammed measured the peak voltage from an ac generator at different rotation frequencies (three trials).

Rotation frequency / Hz | Peak voltage / V: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
5 | 2.10 | 2.10 | 2.10
10 | 3.97 | 4.06 | 4.13
15 | 6.17 | 6.16 | 6.27
20 | 8.32 | 8.25 | 8.25
25 | 9.81 | 10.12 | 10.40

Describe the trend shown by the results and explain it using scientific knowledge.
items.answer: The peak voltage is directly proportional to the rotation frequency. Faster rotation makes the magnetic flux through the coil change more quickly, so the induced voltage is larger (Faraday’s law); the output frequency also equals the rotation frequency.
items.markingKey: 1 trend: The peak voltage is directly proportional to the rotation frequency.; 1 use of data (quote means/values); 1-2 explanation: Faster rotation makes the magnetic flux through the coil change more quickly, so the induced voltage is larger (Faraday’s law); the output frequency also equals the rotation frequency.

items.stem: Zara wants to find out how the number of turns on the secondary coil of a demonstration transformer affects the output voltage. Write a focused research question for this investigation that names both the independent and the dependent variable.
items.answer: How does number of secondary turns affect secondary voltage?
items.markingKey: 1 mark: names the independent variable (number of secondary turns (100, 200, 300, 400, 500) with 200 primary turns); 1 mark: names the measurable dependent variable (secondary voltage measured with an ac voltmeter) in a question form.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "High-voltage dc links should replace ac for long-distance and undersea transmission."

items.stem: Evaluate the claim: "Every country should build a “supergrid” connecting it to its neighbours."
items.answer: Interconnection brings strong benefits for renewables and security, if agreements and investment are in place.

items.stem: "Faraday’s discovery of induction was the most important scientific discovery of the 19th century." To what extent is this view justified?
items.answer: It was among the most important, especially for technology, but “most important” depends on criteria.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: made electricity generation and distribution possible; basis of generators, transformers, motors. items.stem: Write a risk assessment for an investigation into how the rotation frequency of a hand-cranked ac generator affects the frequency and peak voltage of its output. items.answer: Key hazard(s): secure the generator; low voltages only; keep loose clothing away from moving parts. Ethical/environmental: e.g. minimise waste and dispose of chemicals correctly, treat living organisms and volunteers with respect and consent.
